S046.name: Body_Image_Weight_Shape_Disturbance
S046.description: Undue influence of body weight or shape on self-evaluation.

subtypes.Distorted Body Image: Perceiving one's body as much fatter than it actually is or perceiving specific parts as excessively large when looking in the mirror.
subtypes.Self-Worth Dependent on Weight: Judging whether one is a good or successful person solely based on weight or body shape.

S047.name: Compensatory_Behavior_NonPurging
S047.description: Recurrent inappropriate compensatory behaviors to prevent weight gain without purging (direct removal of food).

subtypes.Fasting: Intentionally stopping food intake for a certain period to prevent weight gain.
subtypes.Excessive Exercise: Repetitively performing exercise at a level that exceeds physical limits to prevent weight gain.

S049.name: Eating_Large_Amount
S049.description: Eating, in a discrete period of time, an amount of food that is definitely larger than what most individuals would eat in a similar period of time under similar circumstances.
examples: Eating more than 3-4 times the amount of a typical meal within 2 hours.
Continuously eating large amounts of high-calorie snacks in addition to main meals.
Eating enough to empty a significant portion of the refrigerator or pantry at once.
Eating clearly more food than others during the same period of time.

S050.name: Loss_of_Control
S050.description: A sense of lack of control over eating during the episode (e.g., a feeling that one cannot stop eating or control what or how much one is eating).
examples: A feeling that once I start eating, I cannot stop even if I want to.
Thinking 'I shouldn't eat any more' but mechanically continuing to eat.
A feeling of helplessness that I cannot decide for myself how much to eat.
Eating as if my body is being controlled by someone else.

patient_info.stressor_event: Major change in responsibilities at work (e.g., promotion, demotion)
patient_info.stressor: Joan was asked to serve as grade-level literacy lead while still managing her own classroom, a change that placed her in charge of assessment data, parent updates, and mentoring newer teachers. Across 4 months, the pressure to be exemplary and controlled spread from lesson plans into her eating routines, with repeated private episodes of consuming far more food than she had intended, feeling unable to stop, and then responding with prolonged fasting, extra yoga, or punishingly long trail walks. Her self-evaluation narrowed sharply around weight and shape, especially before staff meetings and classroom observations, making the cycle feel less like stress eating and more like something governing her daily decisions. She eventually used her school district’s employee assistance program to request psychiatric care after recognizing that her carefully structured life had become organized around the binge-and-compensation pattern.

S046.name: Body_Image_Weight_Shape_Disturbance
S046.description: Undue influence of body weight or shape on self-evaluation.
S046.manifestation: If I look even a little softer around my stomach or my pants feel tight before a staff meeting, I honestly feel like I’ve failed at everything, no matter how well my students are doing or how prepared I am.

S047.name: Compensatory_Behavior_NonPurging
S047.description: Recurrent inappropriate compensatory behaviors to prevent weight gain without purging (direct removal of food).
S047.manifestation: After one of those nights, I’ll tell myself I’m not allowed to eat breakfast or lunch at school, and then I’ll stay out on the trail for hours or do extra yoga even when I’m shaky and exhausted.

S049.name: Eating_Large_Amount
S049.description: Eating, in a discrete period of time, an amount of food that is definitely larger than what most individuals would eat in a similar period of time under similar circumstances.
S049.manifestation: I’m here because I keep having these nights where I eat an amount of food that scares me, like I’ll start with leftovers after grading papers and end up going through cereal, crackers, peanut butter, and whatever snacks I packed for my classroom.

S050.name: Loss_of_Control
S050.description: A sense of lack of control over eating during the episode (e.g., a feeling that one cannot stop eating or control what or how much one is eating).
S050.manifestation: Once I start, it feels like the reasonable teacher part of me is watching from the outside saying, 'Joan, stop,' but my hands just keep opening things and putting food in my mouth until I’m painfully full.

additional_requirement_1.name: Additional Requirement 1
additional_requirement_1.description: The binge eating and inappropriate compensatory behaviors both occur, on average, at least once a week for 3 months
additional_requirement_1.manifestation: For the past few months, there has rarely been a week without at least one night where I eat far more than I meant to, and the next day I try to make up for it by not eating at school or pushing myself through a long walk or extra yoga.

functional_impairment.name: Functional Impairment
functional_impairment.manifestation: My evenings and weekends feel planned around undoing what happened with food, so I’ve been slower with grading, less present with friends, and constantly worried about seeming put-together at work.

duration.name: Duration
duration.manifestation: This has been going on for about four months, since I took on the literacy lead responsibilities at school.
